1	//! Maintains a linked list of pages to make up a terminal screen
     2	//! and provides higher level operations on top of those pages to
     3	//! make it slightly easier to work with.
     4	const PageList = @This();
     5	
     6	const std = @import("std");
     7	const builtin = @import("builtin");
     8	const build_options = @import("terminal_options");
     9	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    10	const assert = @import("../quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    11	const fastmem = @import("../fastmem.zig");
    12	const simd = @import("../simd/main.zig");
    13	const tripwire = @import("../tripwire.zig");
    14	const DoublyLinkedList = @import("../datastruct/main.zig").IntrusiveDoublyLinkedList;

    24	const stylepkg = @import("style.zig");
    25	const size = @import("size.zig");
    26	const OffsetBuf = size.OffsetBuf;
    27	const Capacity = pagepkg.Capacity;
    28	const Page = pagepkg.Page;
    29	const Row = pagepkg.Row;
    30	
    31	const log = std.log.scoped(.page_list);
    32	const native_freestanding = builtin.target.os.tag == .freestanding and
    33	    !builtin.target.cpu.arch.isWasm();
    34	
    35	/// The number of pages we preheat the page pool with. For operating systems
    36	/// that support it, pages are demand-paged (see PagePool) so this only
    37	/// costs us address space. For other operating systems, we don't preheat.
    38	const page_preheat = 4;
    39	
    40	/// The number of nodes we preheat the node pool with. Unlike pages, nodes
    41	/// are ordinary heap memory so every idle preheated node costs real
    42	/// memory. A new PageList needs exactly one node for its first page, so
    43	/// we preheat that one and let the pool grow on demand.
    44	const node_preheat = 1;
    45	
    46	/// The number of pins we preheat the pin pool with: the viewport pin that
    47	/// every PageList tracks and the cursor pin that every Screen tracks.
    48	/// Selections, searches, and so on grow the pool on demand.
    49	const pin_preheat = 2;
    50	
    51	/// The list of pages in the screen. These are expected to be in order
    52	/// where the first page is the topmost page (scrollback) and the last is
    53	/// the bottommost page (the current active page).
    54	pub const List = DoublyLinkedList(Node);
    55	
    56	/// A single node within the PageList linked list.
    57	///
    58	/// This isn't pub because you can access the type via List.Node.
    59	const Node = struct {
    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   116	    pub inline fn pageIfResident(self: *Node) ?*Page {
   117	        return switch (self.data) {
